lead: You’ve earned a brain break. Watch this very confident explanation of AI. Spoiler alert: every claim is false. The fun is seeing how wrong it gets.
instructions: Watch the short video and listen for its seven claims.
Select Show Questions when the video ends.
Mark each claim True or False.
heading: Which claims are true?

claims.claim: AI tokens are arcade coins. Every time you ask a question, a tiny robot drops one into a machine. Long questions take a whole bucket.
claims.explain: No coins, no robot. A token is a piece of your text, a word or part of one, and AI turns every piece into numbers before it does anything else.

claims.claim: Training an AI means making it run laps around a data center. The more laps it runs, the smarter it gets.
claims.explain: Training is a loop, not a workout: guess the next word, check, nudge the numbers. Repeat that billions of times, once, before anyone ever asks it a question.

claims.claim: AI adds layers when it gets cold. Bigger models need bigger jackets.
claims.explain: Layers are steps, not jackets. Each one updates the numbers a little more, like rereading a hard sentence until it clicks. Dozens of them, sometimes over a hundred.

claims.claim: AI reads your mind through your cell phone. That’s how its answers sound so personal.
claims.explain: AI can’t read your mind. It sees your message and the context you’ve given it, then predicts likely next words from patterns. Thinking louder won’t help. Typing more will.

claims.claim: Gemini was originally called Lemon Pie. Google changed the name because people kept asking if it came with ice cream, and picked Gemini because it rhymes.
claims.explain: There was never a Lemon Pie. Gemini has been Gemini since Google announced it in 2023. The rhyme is real. Nothing else in that sentence is.

claims.claim: ChatGPT used to be called YellGPT because earlier AI was hard of hearing.
claims.explain: It was never YellGPT, and AI doesn’t hear anything. It reads the text you type. The GPT stands for Generative Pre-trained Transformer, the technology underneath.

claims.claim: Gemini and ChatGPT run on the Transformer, but Claude runs on a special type of pasta called Claude-A-Roni.
claims.explain: Claude runs on the Transformer too, exactly like Gemini and ChatGPT. All three are trained numbers running on computer chips. No pasta, no sauce.
